result.title: VLRLA: Deployment-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language-Action Models through In-Context Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models connect visual perception and language understanding with robot control, providing a foundation for instruction-conditioned manipulation. However, conventional pretrained VLA policies lack a mechanism for gradual adaptation through accumulated interaction experience during deployment. We therefore propose VLRLA, a general framework that equips existing VLA models with \textit{in-context reinforcement learning} capabilities for deployment-time adaptation. Our approach augments a VLA model with a reinforcement learning module that learns from historical observations, actions, rewards, and termination signals. During deployment, the policy gradually refines its action generation and progressively improves task success while keeping model parameters fixed. Our approach is also designed for general applicability and compatibility with diverse learning history construction strategies and model training pipelines. Finally, through extensive experiments, we systematically investigate the learning properties of VLRLA in simulation and demonstrate its ability to adapt to unseen scenarios during real-world deployment.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 VLRLA 框架，在部署阶段用历史观察、动作、奖励与终止信号作为上下文，配合强化学习模块让现有 VLA 策略在不更新参数的前提下逐步改进动作生成，并在仿真与真实部署中验证其适应性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「冻结参数、以历史交互序列构成可更新上下文来改进决策」的机制，可能与 LVR 中 latent 状态的累积更新与利用、以及终止信号驱动的停止/决策设计存在可供核查的借鉴线索。
